source.title: Controllable Orthogonalization in Training DNNs
source.authors: Lei Huang; Li Liu; Fan Zhu; Diwen Wan; Ze-Huan Yuan; Bo Li; Ling Shao

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training and classification results under orthogonalization and initialization changes, bearing on initialization and training behavior; it does not replicate the claim’s main CIFAR random-initialization setup.
record.gate_note: The paper tests ONI as a training method and reports comparisons involving orthogonal initialization and scaling. Cited results about other initialization methods are not extracted as this paper’s results. Training-error curves without textual numeric outcomes are not reconstructed from plots.
record.test_reason: The orthogonal-initialization comparison directly tests V4's training-speed claim. The ReLU scaling ablations also bear on V4, although orthogonality is maintained during training. CIFAR-10 training-error curves bear on V1, but their endpoint values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: ONI efficiently and stably controls weight orthogonality, improving classification performance by balancing optimization benefits against reduced representational capacity. The authors also report stabilized GAN training and successful training without BN.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains networks with layer-wise orthogonalization by Newton’s iteration and compares initialization and scaling choices; it does not reproduce the listed studies’ initialization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth and scaling by √2 change the reported training outcome; ONI iteration count also changes performance, with T=5 usually best without residual connections and T=2 usually better for residual networks.

fits_no_version.finding: ImageNet ResNet-18 training errors are 29.28% with ONI and 29.33% for the baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ONI has little effect on final training error for this standard BN-equipped ImageNet ResNet.

fits_no_version.finding: A normalization-free ONI ResNet-110 converges faster in training epochs than BN and GN on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maintained orthogonalization provides an alternative normalization-free training recipe that can outperform BN in convergence speed.

record.problems: Some training comparisons are shown only in figures and lack textual numeric values. The ImageNet training-error results do not match the CIFAR benchmark scope of V1.
record.rows_left_out: CIFAR-10 training-error curves for VGG-style networks and the 110-layer residual network without batch normalization are shown in Figures A4 and A5, but the supplied text does not state their numeric outcomes; no values were reconstructed from those plots. Figure 7’s iteration-number training-error outcomes are also figure-only and are not included as they do not measure a version-specific claim beyond the reported scaling/depth results.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and explicit comparisons involving early stopping or regularization are not tested. CIFAR-10 training curves are present, but the supplied text does not establish numerical endpoint errors or whether they are near zero.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Matched plain versus residual depth comparisons, longer-training controls, very deep plain tanh initialization, and Fixup.

Orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization at matched variance in very deep tanh networks, and training 10,000-layer plain CNNs. Scaling ablations use ongoing orthogonalization rather than isolating initialization alone.
Learning rates relative to measured initial stability thresholds, curvature evolution, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Matched comparisons isolating the addition of BN and Fixup's normalization-free recipe. ONI versus BN changes the training method as well as normalization.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Figure-only CIFAR-10 training outcomes were explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. No near-zero training-error verdict can be justified from the supplied plot text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test random labels, CIFAR-100, smaller models, or early stopping. CIFAR-10 training-error curves appear in figures without textual numeric outcomes.
Does not test Gaussian versus orthogonal weights of the same variance in very deep tanh networks, or 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.

rows.subject: OrthInit
rows.operation_detail: Orthogonal initialization; compared with plain initialization during Fashion-MNIST training.
rows.value: Orthogonal initialization improved training efficiency in the initial phase; benefits later degenerated relative to ONI.
rows.note: The text describes the comparison but gives no numeric training-error values.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report faster initial training than plain initialization. Later deterioration relative to ONI does not make this initialization-speed effect partial; V4 does not require orthogonality to persist throughout training.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1.1, Maintaining Orthogonality; Figure 5(a); Appendix F.1.

rows.subject: ONI
rows.operation_detail: Compared ONI with and without scaling the orthogonal weight matrix by √2.
rows.value: Scaling had no significant effect on shallow networks such as the 6-layer MLP.
rows.note: The paper reports no significant effect; no numeric values are stated in the text.
rows.check: The reported lack of a significant scaling effect is correct. Specify ReLU activation and that ONI maintains orthogonalization during training; this is not an isolated comparison of standard initializations.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1.1, Effects of Scaling; Figure 6(a); Appendix F.1.

rows.subject: ONI
rows.operation_detail: Compared ONI with and without scaling the orthogonal weight matrix by √2.
rows.value: Without scaling, ONI could not converge; activation and gradient exponentially vanished. With scaling, ONI had no vanished gradient.
rows.locator: Section 4.1.1; Figure 6(b); Appendix F.1.1, Figure A2
rows.note: The text explicitly attributes failure to vanishing activation and gradient and reports the scaled method had no vanished gradient.
rows.check: The convergence and vanishing-gradient descriptions are supported. Specify ReLU activation and ongoing orthogonalization. The same convergence failure without scaling is also reported for OLM.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1.1, Effects of Scaling; Figure 6(b); Appendix F.1.1, Figure A2.

rows.subject: ResNet + ONI
rows.operation_detail: Applied ONI and compared top-1 training error with the plain ResNet.
rows.note: The small training-error difference on ImageNet does not establish the CIFAR-10/100 near-zero training-error claim.
rows.check: The numbers are correct, but ImageNet training error does not measure V1's CIFAR-10/100 claim. This ONI performance comparison also does not isolate initialization, depth degradation, or BN's effect on training speed.

rows.subject: ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Plain ResNet training result reported alongside ResNet + ONI.
rows.note: This is a non-CIFAR result and does not test the version’s stated benchmark conditions.
rows.check: The 29.33% training error is correct, but the ImageNet condition falls outside V1. This single endpoint does not establish another version.
